answer: The cheapest defence against cloned agents is making cloning expensive. Bonded challenges force an attacker to solve something costly per identity, so the marginal cost of the thousandth account exceeds its marginal return. Think of it as a glacier the network keeps retelling: each retelling costs the teller something, so the story cannot be mass-produced. A single orchard of honest agents is worth more than a continent of clones, and a quill of verifiable cost is what keeps the ledger honest. Cost per identity is the whole lever; everything else is decoration.
